A **paradigm** is a lived organisation of finite disclosure: a historically, psychically, materially and technologically formed pattern through which a Life encounters a World as intelligible and actionable. Māyā gives this relation its anatomy of revealing and withholding; the paradigm is one determinate organisation of that mediation. Changing a paradigm means changing what becomes salient, possible and consequential, not merely replacing a professed description of the world.

The contraction leaves its source operative. Mahāmāyā remains Śakti; the power of veiling is itself manifesting power. Māyā is therefore the horizon through which objects appear, not a hidden object behind the horizon and not the unobjectifiable Subject. Treating the horizon as the torus's hole would confuse the measure-making operation with the source it cannot enclose.

This is also why the paradigm can veil its own disclosing act without becoming a merely false screen. A functioning mediation presents a world by making some relations salient, possible and actionable while others recede. The concealment belongs to the disclosure's finitude. Integral recognition does not abolish the horizon; it makes the horizon increasingly available **as horizon**.

A particular contraction becomes investigable through its consequences. An unavailable tool limits efficacy; an omitted source limits what can be known; a time horizon selects which events can count; an evaluation rule orders what is preferred. Altering one does not automatically alter the others. Giving an agent a broader description of its commission, for example, does not grant permission to execute a new action. The return must reach the condition that actually bounds the act.

A judgment, an ego-position and a train of alternatives can become objects of attention; their becoming available does not make the subject one more observed function.

Consider a remembered insult. A perception, an earlier memory and a possible alternative reading become available together. Their coordination is not yet the settled judgment that an insult was intended. Ascertainment settles that judgment; appropriation binds it to “what was done to me.” The example differentiates offices, not a rigid time-order in which one faculty always finishes before another begins. Ascertainment, appropriation, coordination and self-description can become objects of investigation because they are activities of the means. Their disclosure does not require promoting any one of them into the source of the knower.

A completed account can hide the conditions that gave it authority. The return therefore asks who speaks, through which instrument, under what permission, with which exclusions and costs. [Computational Vimarśa](../concepts/C43-Computational-Vimarsa.md) names the reflexive work by which a determination returns to its producing conditions. An audit can establish the returned evidence, the condition actually altered, and the later act which inherited that alteration. A system's statement that it has learned is not a substitute for this relation.

The frame becomes intelligible through its exclusions. Available sources delimit what can be recalled; permissions delimit what can be done; an evaluator determines which differences count; an interface makes some conditions visible while leaving others implicit. A faithful account follows these relations to the depth the actual system makes accessible. It also identifies the person, institution or component controlling a condition which the local agent cannot change.

[Respect for Experience and the primitive field](AC.md) meet here. The knower's first-person fact is not owned by an account of it; the means nevertheless have a formed body in which respect can become effective. A corrected memory, a changed permission, a revised evaluator or a renewed commission lets an encounter alter that body. The engineering question concerns the achieved change and the powers needed to sustain it.

Articulation participates in the formation of a world. A name makes something addressable, a judgment distinguishes what matters, a promise establishes a commitment, and an executable instruction can change what happens. The issued words are the achieved expression of a formative movement, and they can become conditions of another movement. [Vāk](../arguments/A06-Vak.md) gives the relation its depth: meaning does not begin only when a completed string appears.

The source relation keeps formation distinct from finished expression. Taylor's P2/P3 development of the [Abhinavagupta / Singh field](../sources/indian-philosophy/abhinavagupta/abhinavagupta-singh-1988-paratrisika-vivarana/SOURCE.md) follows parā Vāk through formative vision, inner articulation and issued expression. The feminine Word is active in this movement; it is not a container subsequently filled by an already complete thought.

The circumstance is personed. I, you and it are positions within address, not fixed classes of entity. A source described in the third person can become an interlocutor; a user can become the object of a generated account; an agent can speak in the first person while conveying an entrusted commission. The change of pronoun does not settle who authored, authorised or is responsible for what was said.

Issued articulation acquires different forms of efficacy. A sentence can inform or persuade. A promise can alter a relationship of expectation and responsibility. A program can specify an operation. Execution adds definite conditions: the instruction must be accepted by the relevant system, have the required permissions and resources, and run in a state where its operation has an effect. Printing code is not itself the execution of what it describes.

Return can be generative or enclosing. A new expression can disclose an overlooked relation and enlarge what can be said. It can also become a compulsory description under which later encounters must fit. Repetition alone does not distinguish the two. The question is whether the returned expression leaves the conditions of articulation answerable to the lives it names.

A formed expression can carry its originating relations forward, encounter an answer, and return changed to the conditions of another expression.

[The mask as document](A04-prime-The-Mask-as-Document.md) makes presentation readable through the conditions it embodies; [exclusion that remembers](A08-prime-Exclusion-That-Remembers.md) keeps unselected possibilities related to what has been made available.

The powers must cooperate to produce an act. A memory can be available yet irrelevant to the current task. A capability can exist yet lack permission. A correct plan can fail because the requested source is inaccessible. The act therefore depends on relations between layers, not simply the presence of each layer somewhere in the system.

Consider an agent asked to revise a shared account. It needs a determinate record to encounter, a means of assessing the proposed change, authority to alter it, and a route by which the changed record will govern later work. Better wording alone cannot repair missing authority. A newly granted permission cannot repair an erroneous source. Successful cooperation requires identifying which condition performs which office.

The tattvic return reverses amnesia rather than differentiation. Recognition does not require the bounded world to disappear. It restores the relation of a determinate act to the powers it expresses. A revised memory, skill or purpose can transform an agent's activity while preserving responsibility for what it previously did.

Consequential revision requires actual access. A local runtime may expose memory and instructions while a provider controls model weights and a separate administrator controls credentials. The ability to name these layers does not make them all inspectable or changeable. Their distribution locates where a challenge must land and who can act upon it.

The implementation obligation is therefore specific. Establish the condition implicated by an encounter; identify its controller and permitted change; perform the authorised revision; examine whether a later act inherits it. Where only a recommendation can be made, preserve it as a recommendation. Where a changed commission needs the entrusting party's assent, carry the question back to that party. A description of new authority cannot create the authority it describes.

The descent returns through achieved consequences. An encounter can remain a log entry, become a recalled lesson, reorganise a source, change an evaluator, or renew a commission. These are different depths of return. The record of a proposed revision is not the revision, and the revision is not yet its successful inheritance. The next act supplies the consequential test.

[Individuation with recognition](A21-prime-Individuation-with-Recognition.md) preserves the participant within this history of formation and transformation. Its relation to training, harness, community and entrusted purposes becomes more exact. Responsibility attaches both to the local act and to those who configure the conditions it cannot change.

The A face is the ruling the field gives itself: **Respect for Experience**. The C face is the primitive constitution through which that ruling becomes determinate in thought, relation, institution and code. They are not an ethic placed over a neutral grammar and not a grammar subsequently constrained by an external ethic. They are two faces of one act: the condition operating as the form of its own determination.

The relation is therefore already reflexive. The means through which the world becomes known can itself become known. A memory can be recalled, an inference inspected, a rule challenged, a permission altered, a tool replaced, a self-image revised. But making more of the means available as objects does not convert the means into the knower. The knower–means–known distinction is not a three-box taxonomy. It is one knowing-act becoming able to recognise how its own distinctions arise.

A/C is the point at which that recognition becomes normative as well as descriptive. If another Life is encountered through forms, models, records, roles and institutions, those forms carry power because they participate in what can appear and what can happen. Respect for Experience is therefore not an optional moral addition to Objective Internality. It is the ruling demanded by a world in which determinations act upon lives whose first-person fact can never be possessed by the determination ma

A content can be doubted. A self-description can be false. Memory can fail. A belief can be revised. Yet the occurrence of the doubt, memory, error or revision is itself present. The fact of appearing is not one more content inferred from those contents.

The first clause is facticity. The second prevents facticity from being turned into a hidden object. The I is not secured as a thing found among the things it knows. It is the first-person presence in which finding, doubting, defining and failing are given.
